deed: דפנה ניסנבאום מקימה בישראל אריזות מתכלות לחלוטין שמחליפות פלסטיק חד-פעמי
title: Daphna Nissenbaum and Tal Neuman founded TIPA, biodegradable packaging that replaces single-use plastic

trailer.text: Daphna Nissenbaum is an entrepreneur who in 2010, together with Tal Neuman, founded TIPA, an Israeli start-up company that develops fully biodegradable packaging.
Daphna Nissenbaum graduated from the Israeli Army software engineering program and served as an officer in the Israeli Navy software unit.
TIPA is an Israeli start-up company, and according to Green Prophet it was founded by two Israeli women.

They founded the company to address the problem of single-use plastic waste, and it developed flexible, transparent and durable packaging that is fully biodegradable, for fruits, vegetables and dry and baked foods.
According to the company's website, it now serves customers in more than 30 countries, among them Stella McCartney.

glance.label: Scope
glance.value: Customers in more than 30 countries, according to the company

glance.label: Research
glance.value: Two studies at the Volcani Institute

stations.title: An argument over a plastic bottle

paragraphs.text: Nissenbaum said the idea was born from an argument with one of her children about the plastic bottles he took to school.
Before founding the company, she was the CEO of the Caesarea Center for Capital Markets and Risk Management at the Interdisciplinary Center in Herzliya.
According to research cited by the company, nearly 72% of the virgin plastic produced worldwide was used only once before being discarded.
Nissenbaum said that only about 9% of the world's plastic is recycled, 12% is incinerated and 79% goes to landfill.
According to her, most flexible packaging cannot be recycled, and so it remains in landfills for hundreds of years.
She said that even in the European Union, recycling rates for flexible plastic hover around 3%.
Nissenbaum noted that in 2017 China announced it was no longer willing to handle the plastic packaging of the rest of the world's countries.
According to WRAP, the UK disposes of 290,000 tonnes of plastic bags and wrapping every year, and only 6% of it is recycled.
According to an article in Calcalist, food companies cannot continue to use packaging without knowing where it ends its life.
In 2010, Daphna Nissenbaum and Tal Neuman founded TIPA.
The Green Prophet website wrote in 2012 that they were two Israeli women.
According to the same article, three first designs were offered at the time: Tip, Tipack and Tipup.
According to Nissenbaum, one of the hardest things in founding the company was finding partners who believed in the vision.
She said that even when there was a risk of losing the company, she and her team stayed with the core idea: fully biodegradable packaging.
Nissenbaum said that other companies try to shorten the degradation time of existing plastic.
TIPA, according to her, developed a plastic that is compostable from the outset.

stations.title: A bag that turns into soil

paragraphs.text: Nissenbaum said that TIPA makes flexible packaging that looks like snack bags and bags for other food products.
According to the company's website, its films and laminates are certified compostable, and look and feel like conventional plastic.
According to her, the packaging shares the characteristics of conventional plastic and fits existing packaging machinery.

According to the company, the packaging is made of a blend of polymers that turns into full compost within 180 days, and it is intended for industrial composting and in some cases also for home composting.
According to the company, the material contains 20% to 60% plant-based ingredients, such as non-genetically modified corn, depending on the type and shape of the packaging.
According to Nissenbaum, packaging that is buried turns within about half a year into compost suitable for fertilizing soil.
In 2016, Nissenbaum said the company had seven patents surrounding the technology.
In 2022, according to the report, TIPA launched a compostable packaging film called 312MET, which allows thinner packaging.
According to FoodNavigator, the company's chief technology officer said the new film performs like traditional plastic.

stations.title: Cucumbers and peppers in the lab

paragraphs.text: Calcalist reported that a study at the Volcani Institute, in collaboration with TIPA, found that biodegradable packaging extended the life of cucumbers and peppers by about 5 days.
The researchers found a shelf life of up to 21 days for peppers and up to 15 days for cucumbers in the biodegradable packaging.
In storage without refrigeration, biodegradable packaging with tiny holes of the right size kept cucumbers for up to 15 days.
In conventional plastic packaging they lasted 10 days.
The biodegradable packaging also prevented water condensation, which increases rot in vegetables wrapped in conventional plastic.
Both studies determined that TIPA's micro-perforated biodegradable packaging was an equivalent alternative to regular plastic, and even superior to it, for preserving vegetables.
A 2020 survey found that one in three Britons thought fruits and vegetables keep longer when wrapped in plastic.

stations.title: From Israel to markets around the world

paragraphs.text: According to Calcalist, TIPA's products are used to package powders, vegetables, fruits, grains and fresh products.
In 2016, Nissenbaum said the company focuses on flexible packaging for the food industry, a market worth €80.3 billion with no real sustainable solutions.
TIPA works without factories of its own, and collaborates with local factories in America, Australia and Europe.
Nissenbaum said the company has many agents in Europe, and that it recently opened a factory in the US.
According to her, in Australia TIPA produces films, and the company Amcor converts them into packaging and distributes the technology.
According to the company's website, TIPA serves customers in more than 30 countries.
According to Calcalist, the product is not sold in Israel but only to customers abroad, because there is no demand for it in the local market.
According to Food Business News, brands such as Waitrose, Stella McCartney and Juste Bio have adopted TIPA's packaging.
According to the company's website, its customers include Stella McCartney, Sunray and Natura.
According to FreshPlaza, the customers also include Ceres, a company with a vertical farm in Australia, and Sunrays, a producer of grapes sold in the US.
According to the company, TIPA also produces packaging for fashion retailers, among them Stella McCartney, Gabriela Hearst and Mara Hoffman.
Nissenbaum said the fashion industry uses a lot of plastic packaging, and TIPA calls on it to move to compostable solutions.
In September 2019, TIPA raised $25 million, and its total funding to that point reached $49 million.
That year the company was headquartered in Hod HaSharon, and it employed about 40 people.
Nissenbaum said that Millennium invested $4 million in November 2020 and led the latest round.
According to Bizportal, the company reported raising about $70 million, and its total funding since 2010 reached about $130 million.
Among the company's major investors were Blue Horizon of Switzerland, Triodos Bank of the Netherlands, Greensoil Ventures of Canada and Millennium Food-Tech of Israel.
Nissenbaum said that there is currently no plan for an offering in Israel, but she also did not rule out the idea.

The site also noted that for compostable plastic to break down, there must be a sufficient amount of oxygen.

claims.text: ניסנבאום אמרה שענף האופנה צורך הרבה אריזות פלסטיק, ו-TIPA קוראת לו לעבור לפתרונות קומפוסטביליים.
claims.quote: Tipa aims to shift the fashion industry away from plastic packaging and implores it to move toward compostable solutions.

claims.text: בספטמבר 2019 גייסה TIPA 25 מיליון דולר, והסכום הכולל שגויס עד אז עמד על 49 מיליון דולר.
claims.quote: Israel-based compostable plastic company TIPA Corp Ltd. has raised a $25 million funding round, the company announced Monday.

claims.text: סבב הגיוס הוביל לסך גיוסים של 49 מיליון דולר עד אז.
claims.quote: The round brings TIPA’s total funding to date to $49 million.

claims.text: ניסנבאום אמרה שמילניום השקיעה 4 מיליון דולר בנובמבר 2020 והובילה את הגיוס האחרון.
claims.quote: לאחר מכן גייסנו 4 מיליון דולר נוספים ממילניום שהשקיעו בנו בנובמבר 2020

claims.text: לפי ביזפורטל, החברה דיווחה על גיוס של כ-70 מיליון דולר, וסך הגיוסים מאז 2010 הגיע לכ-130 מיליון דולר.
claims.quote: אתמול דיווחה החברה על השלמת גיוס הון נוסף בהיקף של כ-70 מיליון דולר, ובכך גייסה מתחילת הפעילות בשנת 2010 ועד היום סכום של כ-130 מיליון דולר.

claims.text: לפי המשקיעים הגדולים בחברה: בלו הוריזון משווייץ, בנק טריודוס מהולנד, גרינסויל מקנדה ומילניום פוד-טק מישראל.
claims.quote: מבין המשקיעים הגדולים בחברה: בלו הוריזון (שוויץ), בנק טריודוס (הולנד), גרינסויל וונטשרס (קנדה) ומילניום פוד-טק (ישראל).

claims.text: ניסנבאום אמרה שכרגע אין תכנון להנפקה בארץ, אך אין גם פסילה של הרעיון.
claims.quote: כרגע אין תכנון ואין פסילה כזאת. עכשיו אנחנו מתמקדים בלהשלים את המטרות שהצבנו לעצמנו

claims.text: ביקורת: לפי Green Prophet, מוצרים כאלה יהיו חסרי תועלת במדינות שבהן אין תשתית של קומפוסט תעשייתי.
claims.quote: Unless the Environmental Ministry is adequately briefed and establishes a chain of appropriate industrial composting heaps where biodegradable products can slowly disintegrate in optimum conditions, these products will be useless to them.

claims.text: Green Prophet ציין שכדי שפלסטיק קומפוסטבילי יתפרק נדרשת כמות חמצן מספקת.
claims.quote: in order for compostable plastics to biodegrade, it is crucial that they receive adequate amounts of oxygen

claims.text: ב-2016 דיווח FoodNavigator שלחברה יש שותפות עם ארבעה יצרני אריזות וחמישה מותגי מזון באיחוד האירופי ובארה"ב מאז תחילת המכירות בסוף 2015.
claims.quote: The Israel-headquartered company already has already partnered four packaging manufacturers and five food brands across the EU and US since sales launch at the end of 2015.

claims.text: ניסנבאום אמרה שהחברה מוכרת את מוצריה בשוק כבר מ-2017, והשנים הראשונות שימשו בעיקר כפיילוט.
claims.quote: החברה מוכרת את המוצרים בשוק כבר מ-2017. השנים הראשונות היוו בעיקר פיילוט ונועדו להוכיח שהמוצר עובד כמו פלסטיק רגיל בהיבטי השימור

claims.text: ניסנבאום אמרה ש-TIPA מייצרת אריזות גמישות שנראות כמו שקיות חטיפים ומוצרי מזון אחרים.
claims.quote: המוצר העיקרי של TIPA מציע אריזות גמישות, שנראות כמו שקיות של חטיפים או מוצרי מזון אחרים.

claims.text: לפי ניסנבאום, אריזת TIPA מוטמנת ותוך כחצי שנה הופכת לקומפוסט שמתאים לדישון אדמה.
claims.quote: האריזה של TIPA מוטמנת ותוך כחצי שנה היא הופכת לקומפוסט שיכול לשמש לדישון של אדמה

quote_translations.c1: TIPA is an Israeli startup company that was founded in 2010
quote_translations.c28: Biodegradable packaging is at least as effective as conventional plastic (polypropylene) and may even improve the shelf life of fresh produce
quote_translations.c12: Only about 9% of plastic in the world is recycled, 12% of it is incinerated and most of it (79%) goes to landfill
quote_translations.c13: She also notes that already in 2017 China announced that it was no longer willing to handle the plastic packaging of the rest of the world's countries
quote_translations.c14: Food companies are today in a situation where they cannot continue to use packaging without having a way to verify where it ends its life.
quote_translations.c16: Instead of starting the process from scratch and developing the plastic in a way that would allow it to be compostable from the outset, and that is exactly what we did.
quote_translations.c27: According to a study by the Volcani Institute conducted in collaboration with the Israeli start-up company TIPA, biodegradable packaging extended the life of cucumbers and peppers by about 5 days
quote_translations.c29: found that biodegradable packaging allows a shelf life of up to 21 days for peppers and up to 15 days for cucumbers, better results than regular plastic.
quote_translations.c30: In addition, biodegradable packaging with optimal microperforation extended the shelf life of cucumbers without refrigeration to up to 15 days, compared with 10 days in conventional plastic packaging.
quote_translations.c32: An additional advantage of the biodegradable packaging was the prevention of water condensation, which increases the rotting process of vegetables wrapped in conventional plastic.
quote_translations.c31: Both studies concluded that TIPA's microperforated biodegradable packaging was an equivalent and even superior alternative to conventional plastic for preserving vegetables.
quote_translations.c64: A 2020 survey found that one in three Britons believed that fruits and vegetables keep longer when wrapped in plastic.
quote_translations.c19: TIPA's products are used for packaging powders, fresh products, vegetables, fruits and grains
quote_translations.c43: The company has many agents throughout Europe and recently we also opened a factory
quote_translations.c44: Our agreement with Amcor is a bit different in that we produce the plastic films and Amcor then converts them into actual packaging
quote_translations.c33: The company's product is not sold in Israel but only to international customers, due to a lack of demand in the local market.
quote_translations.c41: After that we raised another $4 million from Millennium, who invested in us in November 2020
quote_translations.c42: Yesterday the company reported completing an additional capital raise of about $70 million, and thus from the start of its activity in 2010 to date it has raised a sum of about $130 million.
quote_translations.c46: Among the major investors in the company: Blue Horizon (Switzerland), Triodos Bank (Netherlands), Greensoil Ventures (Canada) and Millennium Food-Tech (Israel).
quote_translations.c45: At the moment there is no such plan and no ruling it out. Now we are focusing on completing the goals we set for ourselves
quote_translations.c34: The company has been selling its products on the market since 2017. The first years were mainly a pilot and were meant to prove that the product works like regular plastic in terms of preservation
quote_translations.c23: TIPA's main product offers flexible packaging that looks like bags of snacks or other food products.
quote_translations.c18: TIPA's packaging is buried, and within about half a year it turns into compost that can be used to fertilize soil
